query: why do I wake up at 3am every night
text: Waking at 3am is common and often tied to normal changes in sleep as we age. Deep sleep tends to shorten and night waking becomes more frequent, so you're more likely to surface in the lighter sleep of the early morning hours. Researchers say the main factors you can control are **shifting melatonin rhythms, caffeine sensitivity, and late-night screen use**, so cutting caffeine earlier in the day and putting screens away before bed may help. Keeping a **consistent wake time** (which matters more than a consistent bedtime) and a **cool bedroom, around 18°C**, can also improve sleep quality. If the waking persists or leaves you exhausted during the day, it's worth talking to a doctor to rule out issues like sleep apnea, stress, or other medical causes.

query: best bedroom temperature for sleep
text: For most adults, the ideal bedroom temperature for sleep is **around 18°C (about 64–65°F)**. A cool room helps you fall asleep faster, partly because your body temperature naturally drops as you drift off. Other things that improve sleep quality include keeping a consistent wake time (which matters more than a consistent bedtime), limiting caffeine, and cutting back on screens late in the evening, especially as sleep tends to get lighter and more broken with age.

query: does caffeine affect deep sleep
text: Yes, caffeine can affect deep sleep. The Northwind Daily article notes that deep sleep naturally shortens with age, and it lists **caffeine sensitivity** as one of the main factors you can control, along with melatonin rhythms and late screen use. It doesn't go into detail about how caffeine works, but research generally shows it can reduce deep (slow-wave) sleep and make you wake more often, even if you still fall asleep easily. Because caffeine stays in your body for several hours (its half-life is roughly 5–6 hours), many sleep experts suggest avoiding it in the afternoon. This may matter more as you get older and become more sensitive to it.

query: how much deep sleep do adults need
text:
The article doesn't give a specific figure, but sleep researchers generally say healthy adults spend about **13–23% of their sleep in deep (slow-wave) sleep**. On a typical 7–9 hours a night, that works out to roughly **1 to 2 hours**. The article notes that deep sleep naturally shortens with age, so people in their forties and beyond often get less, and waking during the night becomes more common. To protect the deep sleep you do get, the article recommends:

- keeping a consistent wake time, which matters more than a consistent bedtime
- keeping your bedroom cool, around 18°C
- watching caffeine intake
- limiting late-night screen use

query: how to check a used EV battery before buying
text: Before buying a used EV, **ask the seller for a recent battery state-of-health (SoH) reading**, which estimates how much capacity remains as a percentage of the original pack. Don't rely on the dashboard range estimate, which isn't a reliable measure of battery condition. Ask about the car's **fast-charging history** and the **climate it was driven in**, since these affect long-term degradation more than mileage does. If the seller can't provide a report, you can get one from a dealer or a third-party testing service. The page I found included a sponsored ad for one such service (VoltCheck), but that was paid advertising, not an independent recommendation.
